title: Migration Orchestra: Cohort-aware preflight + transactional rollback controller for Private VPC
creator: Asha Patel
description: Build a lightweight, safety-first orchestration layer (Migration Orchestra) for Redwood Private upgrades that coordinates preflight checks, cohort selection, transactional state handoff, and staged rollback. The tool will operate as a control-plane service with a pluggable executor for on-prem operators (Helm/K8s job or operatorless SSH runner). Goals: (1) ensure zero-data-loss schema changes via transactional migrators, (2) make canary/cohort selection deterministic and data-residency aware, (3) provide automated gating tied to runtime SLOs and custom policies, and (4) expose clear rollback paths with staleness/lag estimation. This ticket focuses on the design and initial MVP implementation: compatibility heuristics, preflight convergence checks, cohort selector, and a rollback controller that can pause/resume and orchestrate partial rollbacks across stateful components.
acceptance_criteria: A preflight tool can produce a compatibility report for a given Private deployment that enumerates incompatible schema changes, runtime heuristics, and a recommended migration path.
Cohort selector can generate deterministic canary cohorts based on customer size, region, and labels with reproducible hashing and opt-in exclusions.

Rollback controller implements a pause-resume API and can trigger a coordinated rollback plan that targets components by affinity (control plane, database, runtime nodes) and produces a dry-run manifest.
Integration test harness exercises a staged migration (canary -> 20% -> 100%) against a CI cluster; telemetry shows gate evaluation and automated abort on SLO regressions.
Runbook and a first-run playbook are published to Confluence with links to the operator instructions and operatorless SSH runner config.
notes: Trade-offs: prefer simpler deterministic cohorts over ML-based risk scoring for MVP to keep human-auditable rollouts.
We will support both operator-driven (K8s Job/Helm) and operatorless (secure jump-host + signed manifest) executors to cover air-gapped customers.
Telemetry: emit 'preflight:compatibility', 'migration:cohort_selected', 'rollback:initiated' events with correlation_id; link to Console trace for each run.
Safety heuristics: require 3 consecutive successful SLO samples in canary phase before proceeding. Allow configurable policy overrides per-customer.
Long-term: merge Migration Orchestra with release-channel manager for LTS pinning and automated LTS backports.
